Question: Which expression is equal to \[\left|a-2-\sqrt{(a-1)^2}\right|\] for \(a < 0?\)
Solution:
A square root is nonnegative, so \(\sqrt{(a-1)^2}=|a-1|\). The condition \(a<0\) tells us which sign to use: \(a-1<0\), hence \(|a-1|=1-a\).

Substitute this before handling the outer absolute value:
\[
\left|a-2-\sqrt{(a-1)^2}\right|
=|a-2-(1-a)|=|2a-3|.
\]
Since \(a<0\), the number \(2a-3\) is negative. Its absolute value is therefore \(\boxed{3-2a}\), choice A.

Resolve each absolute value using the sign of its entire contents.
